es: Defender una causa local ante un público y responder a una objeción con respeto, evidencia y una petición final.

You are wrong and you do not care about children.
Everyone agrees with me, so stop asking.

feedback.es: Reconoce la preocupación y responde con una comparación; las otras dos atacan a la persona o usan bandwagon.

hint.es: Busca la respuesta que reconoce y luego da una razón.

origin.audio: Some neighbours say a crossing will slow the traffic. I understand the concern. However, two minutes of delay are nothing next to a child's safety.

choices.text: The cost matters and the child matters and so on.
It is possible that maybe the child may cross.
What matters most is not the cost; it is the child who crosses.

feedback.es: Usa un cleft con contraste para destacar la idea clave; las otras frases son vagas.

origin.text: Situación: quieres destacar que la seguridad del niño importa más que el costo.

prompt.es: Decide si la frase del orador es argumento o presión.

choices.text: Misleading: it gives only two options and pressures the listener.
Legitimate: it offers a clear survey result.
Legitimate: it uses a real story about a child.

feedback.es: Finge que solo hay dos opciones y acusa al oyente: es un falso dilema con presión.

origin.text: “Sign now, or you are against our children!”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nunca antes tantos padres habían pedido un paso de peatones.»

answer.text: Never before have so many parents asked for a crossing

feedback.es: Never before al inicio exige el auxiliar have antes del sujeto so many parents.

prompt.es: Identifica el recurso de la pregunta del discurso.

choices.text: A survey result with exact numbers.
A rhetorical question that invites the audience to reflect.
A false dilemma with two options.

feedback.es: La pregunta no espera respuesta: busca que el público reflexione sobre un niño que no puede votar.

origin.text: “Who will speak for a child who cannot vote?”

prompt.es: Escribe tu discurso por el paso de peatones y responde a dos objeciones.

answer.text: Who will speak for a child who cannot vote? This year, three children almost had an accident at our school gate. What we need is a safe crossing. Our survey is clear: 82% of families support it. Some of you may say it will cost too much. I understand your concern, but one accident would cost far more. Others say it will delay the traffic. That is a fair point; however, two minutes of delay are nothing next to a child's safety. Never before have so many parents asked for something so simple. It is our children who cross that road every morning, and it is we who must protect them. Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it is a need. So please sign the petition before Friday, because our children cannot wait.
accepted: Who will speak for a child who cannot vote? This year, three children almost had an accident at our school gate. What we need is a safe crossing. Our survey is clear: 82% of families support it. Some of you may say it will cost too much. I understand your concern, but one accident would cost far more. Others say it will delay the traffic. That is a fair point; however, two minutes of delay are nothing next to a child's safety. Never before have so many parents asked for something so simple. It is our children who cross that road every morning, and it is we who must protect them. Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it is a need. So please sign the petition before Friday, because our children cannot wait.

Imagine a child crossing our road every morning. Three of them almost had an accident this year. A survey found that 82% of families want a safe crossing. I understand the concern about the cost, but one accident would cost much more. It is true that the traffic will slow down; however, two minutes of delay are nothing next to a life. What we need is action, and never before have so many parents asked for it. It is our children who cross that road every morning, and it is we who must protect them. Despite the delay, children will be safer, and the survey shows that families agree. Please sign the petition before Friday.

feedback.es: Un discurso completo abre con un gancho, da el dato del 82 %, responde a cada objeción con respeto y termina con una petición.

origin.text: Datos: paso de peatones seguro frente a la escuela. Este año, tres niños casi fueron atropellados. Una encuesta halló que el 82 % de las familias lo apoya. Objeciones: «cuesta demasiado» y «retrasará el tráfico». Incluye gancho, dato, dos recursos de énfasis, respuesta a las dos objeciones y una petición final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el orador en esta respuesta.

choices.text: He changes the subject to another cause.
He asks the audience to laugh.
He accepts the view, gives data and repeats his request.

feedback.es: Reconoce el punto de vista, cita el dato del 82 % y vuelve a pedir la firma.

origin.audio: You say the road is fine. I understand that. But the survey shows that 82% of parents feel afraid at the gate. So please sign before Friday.
